subtopic: Terraform State Management, Remote Backends and State Locking (DynamoDB)
question_text: [Infrastructure as Code (Terraform / CloudFormation) - Q34] Why is state locking via DynamoDB essential when using an S3 remote backend in a team Terraform environment?

options.text: It speeds up Terraform plan execution by caching state in memory
It prevents race conditions where two engineers or CI pipelines run `terraform apply` concurrently, corrupting the shared remote state file
It encrypts the terraform state file with AES-256

answer_explanation: DynamoDB acts as a distributed lock. When an apply begins, an exclusive lock is acquired in DynamoDB. Concurrent attempts to apply will fail to obtain the lock, preventing catastrophic state file corruption.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: DynamoDB acts as a distributed lock. When an apply begins, an exclusive lock is acquired in DynamoDB. Concurrent attempts to apply will fail to obtain the lock, preventing catastrophic state file corruption.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
